heroHeadline: Denver Court Finds ICE in 'Manifest Noncompliance'; Former GEO Group Executive David Venturella Named Next Acting ICE Director as Senate Prepares Week-of-May-18 $71.7B Reconciliation Vote
heroSubtitle: On May 13, 2026, U.S. District Judge R. Brooke Jackson (D. Colo.) issued an order finding ICE in 'manifest noncompliance' with a November 2025 injunction against warrantless civil immigration arrests — reviewing 36 I-213 arrest records and finding that none complied with the court's documentation requirements. ICE was ordered to complete mandatory training for all officers authorized to make warrantless civil arrests in Colorado within 45 days. The ruling is the latest in a pattern of federal courts documenting ICE defiance of judicial orders. Separately, NPR reported that David Venturella — a former GEO Group government affairs executive — has been named as acting ICE director effective June 1, 2026, when Todd Lyons' resignation takes effect; advocates and Democratic senators raised conflict-of-interest concerns given that GEO Group earns over $700 million annually from ICE detention contracts and stands to receive a windfall under the $71.7 billion reconciliation package up for a Senate floor vote the week of May 18. A Texas Tribune/KSAT investigation published May 13 documented the case of José Contreras Díaz, 30, a Texas DACA recipient illegally deported to Honduras in January 2026 — a federal judge called the deportation a 'flagrant violation' — who was flown back April 29 only to be immediately detained at Port Isabel for 8 days before release May 7. He is one of at least 261 DACA recipients arrested by ICE since January 2025. The Senate's $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation bill — 8× ICE's FY2024 base budget — faces Byrd rule scrutiny of its $1 billion White House ballroom security provision ahead of the May 18 floor vote. FY2026 deaths in ICE custody stand at 30+ at a pace of roughly one every six days.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, court records, and Congressional records
